newsitem.title: UK: Benign US inflation data boosts Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: Benign US inflation data boosts Eurobourses.

text.p: Benign U.S. inflation data on Thursday cooled market speculation of an imminent credit tightening, helped Wall Street bound higher, and boosted European bourses.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 share index cut morning losses and climbed to close at the day's highest levels -- though with a small loss -- after the Dow Jones industrial average opened up and then soon gained about 70 points or more than one percent.

The Dow took heart from Labor Department data showing the crucial core producer price rate rate, which excludes fuel and food, was up only 0.1 percent in December, in line with forecasts and calming fears of an overheating U.S. economy.

The Paris bourse, which had been trading most of the day in the red, also rose into plus figures to close well up and Frankfurt's IBIS DAX electronic trading index ended at a new record after a 1.12 percent rise. German floor trading had closed earlier about half a percent down.

In currency trading, the dollar regained its strength against the mark late in the afternoon, though was still shy of its earlier two-year high of 1.5810 during a session made choppy by a Bundesbank council meeting and a stream of German and U.S. data. It had briefly dipped from its highs against both the mark and the yen after the U.S. data, which was interpreted as meaning there was less pressure for an imminent, dollar-boosting, U.S. rate hike.
Dollar strength was boosted by German data showing a surge in unemployment during December to a postwar high as well as weaker-than -expected 1996 economic growth, widening Germany's budget deficit.
The figures increased speculation that German rates would be trimmed again at some stage but Thursday's regular meeting of the Bundesbank council, as expected, held rates steady.

One concern for mark bulls was the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin, who has been admitted to hospital with pneumonia. Any threat of instability in Russia tends to have a negative effect on the German currency. By late trading in Europe the dollar was trading at around 1.5775 marks.
There were apparently no such worries in Moscow, however, where a raging equities bull market shrugged off the news of Yeltsin's health problems to hit a new record.

Yen weakness was intensified by a continuing freefall in Tokyo stocks, which have slid 11.5 percent since mid-December. The latest overnight tumble Wedensday was sparked by worries that major banks might not solve their huge debt problems amid broader concerns about the health of the Japanese economy.
In late European trading the dollar was quoted at around 116.30 yen, up from late Wednesday's 115.90.
In London equity trading, despite the FTSE index's late recovery, dealers said interest rate worries were still damaging sentiment.

"The bond markets are telling us that British interest rates need to be a half-point higher," said Richard Jeffrey, strategist at Charterhouse Tilney. "The market needs to know what will happen with rates."
German shares had been little moved by the jobless data and it was not until floor business had closed and Wall Street staged its morning rally that post-bourse trading took off on the screens.
One focus of interest was Volkswagen, which surged as management source said an out-of-court settlement with rival GM over their industrial espionage row might be close.

It was a similar story in Paris, which closed three quarters of a percent higher on the back of Wall Street. The index was also boosted by Paribas, which was up 4.02 percent at 354.20 francs after announcing that its Credit du Nord unit would be sold to Societe Generale.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5775 marks and 116.30 yen compared with 1.5758 and 115.90 late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 0.5 points lower at 4,087.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 17.46 at 2,349.08.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 13.71 at 2,892.63 but the IBIS DAX index closed up 32.61 points at 2,936.69, surpassing its previous record peak of 2,916.6 set on December 5.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $355.75, unchanged from its London close of $355.75 on Wednesday. Silver finished five cents firmer at $4.71.
